title: Breakpoint robustness & cross-browser fixups for Console tables, charts, and modals
creator: Ava Mitchell
description: Ensure the Redwood Console UI (dashboards, rollout pages, and cost views) behaves consistently across common breakpoints and browsers. This ticket focuses on robust breakpoint handling for tabular data, chart canvases, and stacked modals: prevent horizontal overflow on tablet/phone widths, avoid chart axis clipping in WebKit, fix modal stacking and focus trapping in Firefox, and stabilize dense row rendering for large tables. Deliver visual QA artifacts, a small component-level CSS guidance doc, and a handoff-ready Figma prototype with annotated breakpoints.
acceptance_criteria: No horizontal page scroll introduced at widths >= 320px (all pages covered: /dashboard, /rollouts, /billing)
Tables collapse gracefully at <= 1024px: secondary columns hide under a ":more" menu and primary actions remain visible
Charts do not clip axis labels in Safari 16+ or produce blurry canvases after resize
Modal stacking and focus trap: nested modals restore focus order and Esc closes topmost modal in Firefox/Chrome/Safari
Sticky table headers align with virtualized row boundaries within 2px on supported browsers
Design sign-off received from PM and Eng; cross-browser visual diff screenshots attached
comments: 2026-03-02 - Initial discovery: repro steps for Safari axis clipping documented; small POC shows axis labels cut when devicePixelRatio != 1
2026-03-04 - Design POC uploaded to Figma (link below). Proposed pattern: column collapse + persistent primary column + overflow menu for secondary metadata
2026-03-06 - Eng synced: ENG-2238 will provide a utility for column priority metadata. Engineering requested designs for both compact and comfortable density
2026-03-08 - Accessibility review: keyboard navigation through collapsed column menu required; ARIA roles and roving tabindex recommended

2026-03-10 - Cross-browser QA pass started on Chrome 120 (Mac/Win), Firefox 115 (Mac/Win), Safari 16 (macOS Ventura). Noted z-index bug in Firefox when modal backdrop uses backdrop-filter; recommendation to remove backdrop-filter for stacked modals

2026-03-12 - Design updates submitted after review: reduced shadow depth to avoid rendering differences, added explicit transform textures for chart canvases to avoid Safari blurring. Ready for engineering handoff
design_notes: Use CSS container queries for card reflow where supported; fallback to legacy media queries for older browsers
Prefer SVG axis rendering for charts where possible; if canvas is required, set explicit width/height attributes and repaint on DPR changes
Column collapse behavior: primary column (name/id) always visible; secondary columns use an inline overflow menu that preserves copy and actions
Avoid backdrop-filter on stacked modals for Firefox; instead use semi-opaque backdrop + subtle inner shadow to maintain perceived depth
Sticky header implementation must account for virtualized lists: use the same transform stack as the virtualization container to avoid visual mismatch
handoff_steps: Finalize Figma frames for 3 breakpoints: desktop (>=1280px), tablet (>=768px <1280px), mobile (<768px)
Export component token changes (spacing, shadows, z-index scale) and add to the design tokens doc
Review with ENG pair (frontend owner + accessibility lead) and schedule 60m handoff session
Attach visual-diff baseline images and list of browsers/OS to smoke-test matrix
notes_for_engineering: ENG ask: prefer a small feature flag for the tablet collapse to rollout progressively
Recommend adding unit-level snapshot tests for the collapsed table cell renderer
For charts: add a resize observer and re-render at the new DPR to avoid Safari aliasing
Ensure keyboard-only flows open/close the overflow menu; test with VoiceOver and NVDA
